findings.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx, the backup code is never sent to the server on login: formSchema is never updated to include backupCode, so zodResolver's plain z.object strips values.backupCode before the unchanged signIn('credentials', ...) call ever runs, leaving credentials.backupCode always undefined and the new backup-code branch in authorize unreachable via the UI; the server answers SecondFactorRequired and the submit handler only re-sets twoFactorRequired(true) with no error message or navigation, so the Sign in button appears dead and the advertised recovery flow is non-functional (and ships untested per the PR's e2e TODO).

In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts (~lines 142-158), backup-code single-use enforcement is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt the code list, indexOf, null the match, then an unconditional prisma.user.update): two concurrent login attempts with the same code (double-submit, two tabs) can both pass indexOf before either write lands, so one code yields two successful logins, violating the 'can be used exactly once' invariant the UI copy promises.

In next-auth-options.ts, the backup code is persisted as consumed before the rest of authorize() runs, so any later failure in the pipeline (org/impersonation checks, a late throw) burns one of only 10 codes without a completed login; consuming the code only after full authorize success would fix this.

In apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~135, ~262), onEnable() only fires from the explicit close button: the Dialog's onOpenChange (X, Escape, outside-click) closes the modal without calling onEnable or resetState, so after enabling 2FA and dismissing with Esc the settings page still shows 2FA off while it's enabled server-side; clicking the switch to enable again makes setup.ts unconditionally overwrite backupCodes and set twoFactorEnabled: false, silently turning 2FA off mid-flow and invalidating the codes the user just downloaded, and reopening the modal lands on the stale DisplayBackupCodes step since resetState is only wired to the footer buttons.

Backup-code matching only strips dashes with no trim or case folding (next-auth-options.ts ~147 and disable.ts ~63): a valid code typed in caps (caps lock, transcribing a printout) or pasted from the downloaded .txt with a trailing newline (which maxLength={11} in BackupCode.tsx:24 preserves as 10 chars + newline) is rejected as 'Backup code is incorrect'; the input should be normalized with trim().toLowerCase().

The null sentinel for consumed codes (next-auth-options.ts ~137/151 and disable.ts ~56) keeps user.backupCodes a non-null string forever, so once all 10 codes are spent every attempt returns IncorrectBackupCode and the intended MissingBackupCodes message ('No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings') can never appear.

The MissingBackupCodes message is unactionable because the PR ships no regenerate-codes UI at all (codes only exist from the enable-setup flow), so pre-existing 2FA users have no way to obtain backup codes short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA.

In DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~38, ~103-111), lost-access mode persists across modal close/reopen: the component stays mounted while the dialog opens/closes and twoFactorLostAccess (and any typed form values) is only reset on success or the explicit buttons, so a user who cancels while in backup-code mode is dumped straight into backup-code mode (with a stale error message if one was set) the next time they open the modal.

In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~272-278), the copy success toast is unconditional: navigator.clipboard.writeText is fire-and-forget, showToast('backup_codes_copied', 'success') shows even if the write rejects (permissions, non-secure origin), and on non-secure contexts navigator.clipboard is undefined and throws synchronously in the handler, so users are told their codes were copied when they weren't.

In packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:47-51, tabIndex={-1} on the password-visibility toggle removes it from keyboard navigation, so keyboard-only users can no longer reach the show/hide password control anywhere it's rendered (login, 2FA setup, disable-2FA password confirmation) — a behavioral regression, not just styling.

In login.2fa.e2e.ts, the always-true assertion flagged by the new FIXME — expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() evaluated on a Promise — means the '2FA enabled' assertion in the first test can never fail, weakening the e2e suite this feature relies on (pre-existing but still unaddressed).

Backup-code login is never wired end-to-end (feature dead-on-arrival): backupCode was added to LoginValues and the rendered form in apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx, but no hunk in the PR updates the login form's zod formSchema (a plain z.object strips unknown keys, so backupCode is removed) or the signIn("credentials", …) call in the submit handler, so backupCode never reaches the server; since the server's backup path (next-auth-options.ts:128) only triggers when credentials.backupCode is truthy, a user with a valid backup code falls through to the TOTP branch and gets SecondFactorRequired — the exact user this feature exists to rescue cannot log in.
The backup-code login path shipped untested — there is no e2e test for logging in with a backup code (the PR's own TODO 'add more backup code tests, e.g. login…' acknowledges this gap).

Backup-code consumption in next-auth-options.ts:128-153 is non-atomic (decrypt → indexOf → backupCodes[index] = null → re-encrypt → unconditional prisma.user.update) with no transaction, conditional update, or version check: two concurrent sign-ins with the same code both read the original ciphertext and both succeed (one code yields two logins), and concurrent logins with different codes can lose the first null-out, resurrecting an already-used code — violating the promised 'Each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee.
The backup code is invalidated (burned) before authorize() finishes, so any later failure in the sign-in flow destroys a valid code without granting access.

Backup codes have only 40 bits of entropy — crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex") in totp/setup.ts yields 10 hex chars — below industry standards (GitHub's 10-char codes ≈ 52 bits); with 10 simultaneously valid codes, an attacker who already holds the account password needs only ~2³⁷ expected guesses to bypass TOTP via the backup path.

The new backup-code verification paths (login authorize and disable.ts) have no dedicated failure counter or lockout, so backup-code guessing is bounded only by whatever generic login rate limiting happens to wrap the endpoint.

Users who enabled 2FA before this deploy have backupCodes = null, and the MissingBackupCodes error misleads them by directing them to 'generate them in your settings' when no such regeneration flow exists — the only way to obtain codes is to disable and re-enable 2FA, which itself requires a working TOTP, producing a recovery dead-end and support-driven lockouts.
Backup codes are displayed exactly once with no view/regenerate action, so a user who closes the dialog without copying or downloading them is permanently stuck with codes they've never seen.

In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the blob URL created with URL.createObjectURL is never revoked when the dialog closes or on unmount — it is only revoked when a new setup run replaces it — so a live object URL backed by a Blob containing the plaintext backup codes persists for the entire document lifetime

resetState() in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx clears password/error/step but leaves backupCodes and backupCodesUrl intact, so plaintext backup codes remain resident in React state after the user closes the modal and a working download link to the codes stays valid

Backup-code consumption in next-auth-options.ts (~145-155) is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → set null → re-encrypt → prisma.user.update) with no transaction or conditional update, so two concurrent authorize calls submitting the same code both read the same stored list, both pass indexOf, and both update — allowing a single-use code to grant two sessions

In next-auth-options.ts, the backup code is burned at verification time before next-auth has actually created the session, so any downstream failure in the auth pipeline consumes one of the user's 10 codes without granting access

Backup code login can never succeed: the diff never adds `backupCode` to the zod `formSchema` used by `zodResolver` or to the `signIn("credentials", ...)` call in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`, so the field is stripped before reaching the provider, the TOTP branch runs with an empty `totpCode`, and the recovery flow silently fails with no visible error or test coverage

Existing 2FA users with `backupCodes = NULL` get a dead-end `missing-backup-codes` error on login and 2FA disable that tells them to 'generate them in your settings,' but no regenerate endpoint exists and generating codes requires completing the enable flow with the TOTP code they no longer have — a rollout/back-compat gap for the entire installed base of 2FA users

`onEnable()` in `apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` now only fires from the 'close' button on the backup-codes step; closing via Esc or the dialog X skips it, leaving the parent's 2FA switch showing 'disabled' while the DB has 2FA enabled (state desync) and irreversibly dismissing the one-time backup codes since no endpoint exists to re-display them

Backup-code consumption is not atomic: the code decrypts, nulls one index, and re-encrypts the entire array via a non-transactional `prisma.user.update`, so two concurrent sign-ins with the same backup code both pass the check (granting two sessions) and concurrent use of different codes can clobber each other's consumption via last-write-wins, violating the single-use contract

PasswordField reveal toggle in `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx` was given `tabIndex={-1}`, removing the show/hide password button from keyboard tab order for every consumer across all apps, a WCAG 2.1.1 accessibility regression for keyboard-only users

The new e2e assertion in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` — `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` — asserts on a Promise object which is always truthy, so the test passes whether or not the 2FA switch is checked and proves nothing about 2FA being enabled

Backup-code login can never succeed: `backupCode` is never sent to the credentials provider — the `signIn()` call site and zod `formSchema` are unchanged (and `zodResolver` strips unknown keys), so `credentials.backupCode` is always `undefined`, authorize falls into the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired` (a no-op on the client); a user with a valid backup code sees nothing happen and stays locked out, and the new `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes` branches in login.tsx are dead code

Single-use backup-code enforcement is a check-then-act race with no transaction, row lock, or atomic compare-and-update: two concurrent sign-ins with the same code can both pass `indexOf` before either write lands (one single-use code grants two logins), and two different codes used in parallel mean last-write-wins resurrects an already-consumed code

Clipboard copy in `EnableTwoFactorModal` (`backup-codes-copy` onClick) has no error handling: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is neither awaited nor caught and the success toast fires unconditionally — on permission denial the promise rejects unhandled while the toast falsely claims success, and on insecure (plain-HTTP) contexts `navigator.clipboard` is undefined causing a synchronous throw with no toast at all

No re-display or regeneration path for backup codes: codes are minted only in `setup.ts` and displayed exactly once in client state, so closing the dialog via X/Esc/backdrop or refreshing after `handleEnable` permanently loses unsaved codes; the `MissingBackupCodes` message tells users to generate codes in settings but no code implements this, creating an unrecoverable lockout for accounts with `backupCodes = null` (and pre-deploy 2FA users)

Dialog-dismissal paths never reset modal state: `resetForm`/`resetState` are only wired to explicit toggle and Close/Cancel buttons, so Esc, backdrop, X, or the Disable modal's Cancel leave `twoFactorLostAccess`, `errorMessage`, form values, and `step` stale, making reopening show the wrong mode or stale errors; at `DisplayBackupCodes`, X/Esc skip `onEnable()`, leaving the parent switch rendering "off" while 2FA is actually enabled until a refresh

Missing-encryption-key path in `disable.ts` throws `new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` instead of returning a JSON error, producing a Next.js 500 with a non-JSON body so the client's `await response.json()` throws and the user gets the generic catch-all instead of a mapped error

`.replaceAll()` on unvalidated user input in `disable.ts` (and the same pattern in `next-auth-options.ts`) can crash the endpoint with a 500: `req.body.backupCode` is used directly as a string with no type check or schema validation, so a body like `{"backupCode": 123}` throws a TypeError instead of returning a 400

Case-sensitive backup-code comparison with no input normalization: codes are lowercase hex but the input lacks `autoCapitalize="none"`/normalization and the placeholder is uppercase, so iOS Safari's default sentence autocapitalization causes a hand-typed valid code to fail with "Backup code is incorrect" in the one-shot recovery flow

The e2e test assertion `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` can never fail: it passes a Promise to a synchronous matcher, which is always truthy regardless of switch state, so the extended enable-flow test provides zero regression protection; it should be `expect(await ...isChecked()).toBe(true)`

No test coverage for backup-code login, the feature's core purpose: the TODO at apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 acknowledges the core flow is untested, leaving untested the lost-access toggle and TOTP/backup go-back behavior in login.tsx:104-135, the authorize branch in next-auth-options.ts:131-157 (valid code logs in and is consumed; invalid → IncorrectBackupCode; backupCodes = null for pre-migration users → MissingBackupCodes), and the new error mappings at login.tsx:156-157

No test coverage for disabling 2FA with a backup code: DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:103-118 (lost-access toggle, resetForm(false) keeping password while clearing codes), the backup branch in disable.ts:46-64 including dash-stripping, and the backupCodes: null wipe at disable.ts:107 — nothing verifies stored codes become unusable after disable

One-time-use invariant of backup codes is untested: no test asserts a reused code is rejected or that remaining codes still work after one is consumed (next-auth-options.ts:148-157 null-out-and-re-encrypt consumption is the security guarantee); test plumbing (builder.ts:192 backupCodes: null) was added but no authorize tests cover the new branch

The e2e never asserts actual backup code values: no assertion on the displayed grid (count = 10, format XXXXX-XXXXX guarding formatBackupCode's slice logic), the download test only checks suggestedFilename() (from the anchor's download attribute, verifying markup not data), and the clipboard TODO is unaddressed — empty or malformed generated codes would pass every test

navigator.clipboard.writeText is not awaited and showToast runs unconditionally in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~283-287, so a denied clipboard (headless CI, insecure context, iframe) still shows 'Backup codes copied!' with nothing copied — and the e2e asserts exactly that toast, passing in precisely the environments where the feature is broken

Vacuous assertion left unfixed in login.2fa.e2e.ts:47-50: `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts a Promise (always truthy) and always passes; it should be `await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()` — this is the primary enable test's success signal, leaving the '2FA is on' state unverified

No negative-path tests for the new disable.ts backup branch: IncorrectBackupCode (400), MissingBackupCodes (400), and symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse failures (key rotation, corrupt data) are all uncovered and currently unhandled

A non-string body value for backupCode (e.g., {"backupCode": 123}) hits req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...) in disable.ts (~line 60), throwing a TypeError and resulting in an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 — no schema validation is visible in the handler

No integration test for setup.ts code generation/persistence: nothing asserts exactly 10 codes of 10 hex chars, that codes are stored encrypted (an at-rest plaintext regression would be invisible to the e2e), or that re-running setup regenerates codes and invalidates any previously displayed/saved set

Dismissing the backup-codes step via the dialog X / onOpenChange path (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:258-283) calls neither resetState() nor onEnable(), unlike the 'close' button — leaving step stale so reopening the modal shows the old codes step instead of password confirmation, and skipping onEnable() so the settings switch may not reflect the enabled state until refresh; no test covers X dismissal at any step

No input normalization of user-entered backup codes: neither the client (BackupCode.tsx:19-27, raw register with no trim) nor the servers (next-auth-options.ts:144, disable.ts:60) normalize whitespace or case before exact-match indexOf against lowercase hex, so a trailing space from paste or manually uppercase entry (the placeholder XXXXX-XXXXX suggests uppercase while codes are lowercase hex) rejects a valid code with 'Backup code is incorrect.'

Backup-code verification logic duplicated across two server entry points (next-auth-options.ts:131-148 and totp/disable.ts:46-62), with a third diverging site in setup.ts:60-67 that encrypts without the env-key guard the others added; the copies have already diverged (login nulls and re-persists the consumed code, disable doesn't), so security-critical logic that must change in lockstep lives in three places — extract a shared verify/consumeBackupCode() lib function

Backup-code format knowledge (code length, dash position, normalization rules) is scattered across 5+ locations with no single source of truth; normalization is already asymmetric — dashes are stripped server-side but case is not, so a user typing an uppercase code fails the server-side exact-match indexOf — extract a shared constant/format util

BackupCode.tsx exports a component named TwoFactor, creating a naming conflict with another auth component default-exported under the same name; every import must be aliased and IDE auto-import/stack traces point to the wrong file — rename the function to match the file

Dialog exit paths bypass reset logic: in EnableTwoFactorModal the onOpenChange path (X button, Esc) calls neither resetState() nor onEnable(), so closing at the DisplayBackupCodes step silently skips onEnable() and leaves stale step/secret state; DisableTwoFactorModal's plain onCancel similarly skips resetForm(), retaining stale error and form values — reset should be centralized in the open/close lifecycle, not per-button handlers

Error message references a feature that doesn't exist: the 'missing_backup_codes' locale string instructs users to generate codes in their settings, but there is no settings UI or endpoint to generate/regenerate backup codes, leaving pre-migration 2FA users and users who exhausted all 10 codes at a dead end

resetState in EnableTwoFactorModal is incomplete and leaks the blob URL: it clears only 3 of 8 state fields, leaving backupCodes (sensitive) lingering in memory after close, and URL.revokeObjectURL is only called when replacing a prior URL — the last URL is never revoked on reset or unmount

useState([]) in EnableTwoFactorModal infers never[] instead of the intended string[]; it only compiles because body is any from response.json(), and any future typed interaction with this state produces confusing errors — should be useState<string[]>([])

DisplayBackupCodes close/copy buttons render inside the enable <Form> and avoid re-submitting the TOTP enable only via manual e.preventDefault(), a fragile coupling; the download control nests a <Button/> inside an <a>, which is invalid HTML (nested interactive elements) sitting inside the form

Lost-access toggle UI duplicated in login.tsx TwoFactorFooter and DisableTwoFactorModal with drifting implementations: the modal conditionally preserves the password while login doesn't, and login special-cases two new error codes with inline if/else instead of extending its existing errorMessages map — extract a shared wrapper component

Auth-mode is encoded by field presence with three positional string params: disable(password, code, backupCode) is transposition-prone (swapping code/backupCode compiles and silently changes behavior) and 'empty string means TOTP' is an implicit, undocumented protocol — use an explicit discriminator or object param

Null-hole consumption representation conflates 'missing' with 'exhausted': consumed codes become null placeholders in a JSON blob, so once all 10 are used the column is a truthy string, MissingBackupCodes can never fire again, and exhausted users get 'Backup code is incorrect.'

Exported shared auth components BackupCode.tsx and TwoFactor.tsx declare untyped props (only loosely inferred from defaults), and the PR extends that surface with autoFocus; components consumed by three call sites need an explicit Props type contract

Core new flows ship untested: login-with-backup-code and disable-with-backup-code (the primary new behaviors, including single-use consumption) have no coverage, and the FIXME at playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-51 leaves in a known-broken assertion (isChecked() check that passes when it shouldn't), verifying nothing

Backup-code login is likely dead-on-arrival: the zod form schema in apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx does not include the new backupCode key and strips unknown keys by default, so zodResolver drops the credential before the signIn('credentials', ...) call reaches next-auth-options.ts — the server sees no backupCode and empty totpCode, returns SecondFactorRequired, and login.tsx just calls setTwoFactorRequired(true) (a no-op) with no error message, a silent failure on the feature's headline flow. Update formSchema (or make it passthrough), update the signIn payload, and add the missing e2e test.

Backfill gap: existing 2FA users have backupCodes = NULL and no way to generate them — the 'Lost access' flow returns MissingBackupCodes and tells users to generate codes in settings, but no such flow exists (the only code generator is the enable flow in setup.ts, which is unreachable while 2FA is on and forcibly sets twoFactorEnabled: false, so it is not a regeneration path either). Ship a 'regenerate backup codes' action or a backfill that provisions and delivers codes to existing 2FA-enabled users.

One-time-use guarantee is not atomic (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:143-158): the consume step is decrypt → indexOf → set the entry to null → re-encrypt the whole array → user.update, with no transaction or conditional write. Concurrent sign-ins with the same code can both pass indexOf before either writes (classic TOCTOU, code used twice), and concurrent sign-ins with different codes each serialize a full stale array so the second write resurrects the code the first just consumed, violating the locale string's 'Each backup code can be used exactly once' promise. Fix with a transaction plus conditional update, or store one row per code with an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE code = x AND used = false.

Backup code is burned before authentication completes (next-auth-options.ts:149-158): the destructive user.update runs immediately after the code matches, but authorize must still return and next-auth must complete session/JWT creation (plus any later checks such as rate limiting or org/email-verification) — any failure after the burn consumes one of the 10 limited codes without granting access. Consume the code only after the full sign-in succeeds, or accept and document the lossy semantics.

apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:47-50 throws raw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) in the missing-encryption-key branch instead of returning JSON, producing an unhandled 500 with a non-JSON body so the client's await response.json() (DisableTwoFactorModal handleDisable) throws into the generic catch — inconsistent with sibling branches that return res.status(4xx).json({ error }). Return a proper 400/500 JSON error instead.
The console.error text in the disable endpoint says 'backup code login' on the disable flow — a copy-paste error producing a misleading log message.

The e2e assertion in apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:49-52 can never fail: 'await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()' asserts on a Promise object, which is always truthy, so the check passes regardless of the 2FA switch's actual state, leaving a knowingly-vacuous assertion that gives false confidence on the core enable flow. Replace with 'await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()'.

The Dialog's X close affordance at the backup-codes step in apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx bypasses onEnable: onOpenChange presumably routes to the parent's cancel path, so closing via X after 2FA was enabled server-side never notifies the parent, leaving the settings switch showing a stale 'off' state until a refetch (previously impossible because onEnable fired before any close). Make onOpenChange at this step also call onEnable, or have the parent refetch on close.

Login page never transmits backupCode to signIn("credentials") — the zod formSchema (with zodResolver stripping undeclared keys) was not updated to include the new backupCode field, so credentials.backupCode is always undefined in authorize(), the server takes the TOTP branch and returns SecondFactorRequired, and the 'lost access' backup-code login path silently fails with no error or feedback (dead code in error branches for IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes)

TOCTOU race in backup code burn: non-atomic read-modify-write (indexOf → set to null → re-encrypt → prisma.user.update) allows two concurrent sign-ins with the same code to both succeed, violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee — needs a conditional/atomic update so only one request wins

Backup code is consumed inside authorize() before the session/JWT/cookie is actually created — if anything fails after the burn (JWT/session callbacks, dropped response, cookie not persisted), the user is not logged in but the code is destroyed, and retrying yields IncorrectBackupCode for a valid code; consumption should be tied to actual sign-in completion or be retriable

Error message tells users to 'generate them in your settings' but no backup code regeneration endpoint/UI exists in the PR — users who enabled 2FA before the migration have backupCodes = NULL (nullable column, no backfill) and can never obtain codes, and codes are shown only once in EnableTwoFactorModal with no way to re-view them

EnableTwoFactorModal state is only reset via Cancel/Close footer buttons — dismissal via X button, Escape, or overlay click passes through onOpenChange leaving stale step/password/backupCodes/secret state, and X-dismissal after successful enable skips onEnable() so the parent thinks 2FA is disabled and re-running setup silently rotates the already-saved codes

E2e assertion always passes: `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise object which is always truthy, so the '2FA is enabled' check passes instantly whether or not the switch is checked — should use toBeChecked() instead

Unvalidated req.body.backupCode crashes the disable endpoint: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes a string, so a JSON body like {"backupCode": 5} throws a TypeError and returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 validation error

Backup code input is not normalized for case and whitespace — server only strips dashes with no .toLowerCase() or .trim(), so uppercase entry (invited by the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder) or paper-transcribed/pasted codes with stray whitespace are falsely rejected as 'Backup code is incorrect'

Copy button shows the 'Copied!' success toast unconditionally — navigator.clipboard.writeText is fire-and-forget and showToast runs immediately regardless of rejection (insecure context, missing permissions, unavailable clipboard API), falsely telling the user codes are saved with no way to view them again

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx, the backup code is never sent to the server on login: formSchema is never updated to include backupCode, so zodResolver's plain z.object strips values.backupCode before the unchanged signIn('credentials', ...) call ever runs, leaving credentials.backupCode always undefined and the new backup-code branch in authorize unreachable via the UI; the server answers SecondFactorRequired and the submit handler only re-sets twoFactorRequired(true) with no error message or navigation, so the Sign in button appears dead and the advertised recovery flow is non-functional (and ships untested per the PR's e2e TODO).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `backupCode` to `LoginValues` and renders `<BackupCode center />`, which registers `methods.register("backupCode")`, but there is no corresponding diff updating the login form’s Zod `formSchema` used by `useForm({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })`. With a typical `z.object(...)` schema, unknown keys are stripped during parsing, so `backupCode` can be dropped before submission and thus never reach the `signIn('credentials', ...)` call. That would make the new `credentials.backupCode` branch in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` effectively unreachable from this UI, matching the reported “dead” recovery flow behavior when `SecondFactorRequired` is returned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts (~lines 142-158), backup-code single-use enforcement is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt the code list, indexOf, null the match, then an unconditional prisma.user.update): two concurrent login attempts with the same code (double-submit, two tabs) can both pass indexOf before either write lands, so one code yields two successful logins, violating the 'can be used exactly once' invariant the UI copy promises.
matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same race condition: backup codes are decrypted and modified in memory with a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent login attempts using the same backup code can both pass the check before either update is persisted, allowing a one-time code to be reused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In next-auth-options.ts, the backup code is persisted as consumed before the rest of authorize() runs, so any later failure in the pipeline (org/impersonation checks, a late throw) burns one of only 10 codes without a completed login; consuming the code only after full authorize success would fix this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in `next-auth-options.ts` the backup code is marked as used and persisted (`backupCodes[index] = null; await prisma.user.update(...)`) immediately after verifying it, before the rest of `authorize()` completes (the function continues afterward in the `else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)` branch and presumably toward a final return). The diff does not show the remainder of `authorize()` or the wider NextAuth pipeline, so we cannot conclusively verify that a later failure/throw can occur after this point in this PR; however, the ordering does introduce a real risk of consuming a code even if login ultimately fails later, making it a concrete, diff-grounded design/edge-case concern rather than a proven defect from the visible changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~135, ~262), onEnable() only fires from the explicit close button: the Dialog's onOpenChange (X, Escape, outside-click) closes the modal without calling onEnable or resetState, so after enabling 2FA and dismissing with Esc the settings page still shows 2FA off while it's enabled server-side; clicking the switch to enable again makes setup.ts unconditionally overwrite backupCodes and set twoFactorEnabled: false, silently turning 2FA off mid-flow and invalidating the codes the user just downloaded, and reopening the modal lands on the stale DisplayBackupCodes step since resetState is only wired to the footer buttons.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, after a successful enable request it now does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` instead of calling `onEnable()` (see handleEnable). The only place that calls both `resetState()` and `onEnable()` is the explicit “close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes footer (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`). The Dialog itself is controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange` props, and this component does not hook `onOpenChange` to call `resetState()` or `onEnable()`. So closing via Dialog chrome (X), Escape, or outside click can dismiss the modal without firing `onEnable()` and without resetting internal `step/password/errorMessage`, leaving stale UI state and potentially a stale parent UI that depends on `onEnable()` to refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code matching only strips dashes with no trim or case folding (next-auth-options.ts ~147 and disable.ts ~63): a valid code typed in caps (caps lock, transcribing a printout) or pasted from the downloaded .txt with a trailing newline (which maxLength={11} in BackupCode.tsx:24 preserves as 10 chars + newline) is rejected as 'Backup code is incorrect'; the input should be normalized with trim().toLowerCase().

The null sentinel for consumed codes (next-auth-options.ts ~137/151 and disable.ts ~56) keeps user.backupCodes a non-null string forever, so once all 10 codes are spent every attempt returns IncorrectBackupCode and the intended MissingBackupCodes message ('No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings') can never appear.

adjudication.rationale: In `next-auth-options.ts`, successful backup-code auth sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts/updates the column (`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...)`). That means `user.backupCodes` remains a non-null encrypted JSON string even after all codes are consumed (array becomes all `null`). Future attempts will decrypt and run `backupCodes.indexOf(<string>)`, which will return `-1` and throw `IncorrectBackupCode`, while `MissingBackupCodes` is only thrown when `user.backupCodes` is falsy (`if (!user.backupCodes) ...`). So the “missing_backup_codes” path cannot trigger for the “all codes spent” state; it will always look like an incorrect code. (The cited `disable.ts` doesn’t use the null-sentinel pattern, but the underlying issue is real in the login flow.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code consumption in next-auth-options.ts:128-153 is non-atomic (decrypt → indexOf → backupCodes[index] = null → re-encrypt → unconditional prisma.user.update) with no transaction, conditional update, or version check: two concurrent sign-ins with the same code both read the original ciphertext and both succeed (one code yields two logins), and concurrent logins with different codes can lose the first null-out, resurrecting an already-used code — violating the promised 'Each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup-code path (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)`) performs a read-modify-write sequence on `user.backupCodes`: decrypt → `indexOf` → mutate `backupCodes[index] = null` → `prisma.user.update` with re-encrypted JSON. The update has no transaction, no conditional `where` clause tied to the prior ciphertext/value, and no optimistic locking/version check. Two concurrent sign-ins can both read the same original encrypted value and both pass `indexOf(...) !== -1` before either write commits, allowing the same backup code to be accepted more than once; concurrent logins using different codes can also clobber each other’s null-outs (lost update). This violates the UI promise added in `common.json` (“Each backup code can be used exactly once…”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The backup code is invalidated (burned) before authorize() finishes, so any later failure in the sign-in flow destroys a valid code without granting access.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode`, the code is immediately invalidated by writing `backupCodes[index] = null` and persisting it via `prisma.user.update(...)` before `authorize()` completes/returns the user. This means any subsequent error/throw within `authorize()` after that point, or any later NextAuth sign-in failure after `authorize` returns (session/JWT/callback failures), can result in a burned backup code without a successful login, causing irreversible loss of a valid code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes have only 40 bits of entropy — crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex") in totp/setup.ts yields 10 hex chars — below industry standards (GitHub's 10-char codes ≈ 52 bits); with 10 simultaneously valid codes, an attacker who already holds the account password needs only ~2³⁷ expected guesses to bypass TOTP via the backup path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code generation in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` as `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, which produces 10 hex characters per code (40 bits of entropy). The diff also returns/stores 10 such codes (`Array.from(Array(10), ...)`) and allows bypassing TOTP using `credentials.backupCode` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` and `req.body.backupCode` in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`. This makes the backup-code path a second-factor alternative with relatively low brute-force space per valid code, and having multiple simultaneously valid codes further reduces effective guessing effort. This is a concrete security weakness introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new backup-code verification paths (login authorize and disable.ts) have no dedicated failure counter or lockout, so backup-code guessing is bounded only by whatever generic login rate limiting happens to wrap the endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new backup-code authentication branches in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode) { ... }`) and in the disable endpoint `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode) { ... }`). In both places, the added logic only checks membership in the decrypted backup-code list and returns/throws on mismatch; it does not add any attempt counter, throttling, or lockout specific to backup-code failures. Whether generic/login-wide rate limiting exists elsewhere isn’t shown in the diff, so the review point is best treated as a scoped security hardening concern rather than a strictly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Users who enabled 2FA before this deploy have backupCodes = null, and the MissingBackupCodes error misleads them by directing them to 'generate them in your settings' when no such regeneration flow exists — the only way to obtain codes is to disable and re-enable 2FA, which itself requires a working TOTP, producing a recovery dead-end and support-driven lockouts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces backup-code-based recovery paths (e.g., login UI toggle `lost_access` and `BackupCode` input; API checks in `next-auth-options.ts` and `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`). However, existing 2FA users will have `backupCodes` as NULL (new nullable DB column, no backfill). When such a user attempts the new backup-code path, both login and disable flows can return `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` (e.g., `if (!user.backupCodes) throw/return MissingBackupCodes`), and the UI message says to generate them in settings. In this diff, backup codes are only generated in the 2FA setup endpoint (`totp/setup.ts`) and surfaced in the enable modal after enabling; there is no shown regeneration/backfill path for already-enabled users, making the new recovery option effectively unusable for that cohort and the message misleading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are displayed exactly once with no view/regenerate action, so a user who closes the dialog without copying or downloading them is permanently stuck with codes they've never seen.

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, backup codes are generated server-side during `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` and only surfaced in the UI in the one-time `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` step (rendered as a grid with copy/download/close actions). There is no code in this diff that provides a later “view backup codes” or “regenerate backup codes” path anywhere in settings, and the API does not expose any endpoint to fetch them again. So if the user dismisses the modal without copying/downloading, they may not be able to retrieve those codes later (even though they still exist in `users.backupCodes`). This is a UX/product gap rather than an immediate correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code consumption in next-auth-options.ts (~145-155) is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → set null → re-encrypt → prisma.user.update) with no transaction or conditional update, so two concurrent authorize calls submitting the same code both read the same stored list, both pass indexOf, and both update — allowing a single-use code to grant two sessions

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code consumption is implemented as a read-modify-write sequence: decrypt `user.backupCodes` → `indexOf(credentials.backupCode...)` → set `backupCodes[index] = null` → `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) }})`. adjudication_records.issue_text: In next-auth-options.ts, the backup code is burned at verification time before next-auth has actually created the session, so any downstream failure in the auth pipeline consumes one of the user's 10 codes without granting access

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, within the Credentials provider `authorize`, the code verifies `credentials.backupCode` and then immediately mutates persistence by nulling that code and calling `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } })` before the auth flow completes. Since `authorize` runs prior to NextAuth finishing the sign-in/session creation (it must still return the user and proceed through NextAuth’s subsequent steps), any downstream failure after this DB write (e.g., an exception thrown after the update, or later NextAuth pipeline failure) would leave the user without a valid session while still having consumed a one-time backup code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code consumption is not atomic: the code decrypts, nulls one index, and re-encrypts the entire array via a non-transactional `prisma.user.update`, so two concurrent sign-ins with the same backup code both pass the check (granting two sessions) and concurrent use of different codes can clobber each other's consumption via last-write-wins, violating the single-use contract

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login performs a read-modify-write on `user.backupCodes`: it decrypts (`symmetricDecrypt`), checks `indexOf(...)`, mutates `backupCodes[index] = null`, then persists via a plain `await prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } })`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code login can never succeed: `backupCode` is never sent to the credentials provider — the `signIn()` call site and zod `formSchema` are unchanged (and `zodResolver` strips unknown keys), so `credentials.backupCode` is always `undefined`, authorize falls into the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired` (a no-op on the client); a user with a valid backup code sees nothing happen and stays locked out, and the new `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes` branches in login.tsx are dead code

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `backupCode` field to the Credentials provider (`next-auth-options.ts` adds `backupCode` and `authorize` checks `credentials.backupCode`) and adds a BackupCode input to the login UI (`login.tsx` + `BackupCode.tsx` registers `backupCode`). However, in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` the only changes shown are UI/state/error-branch additions; there are no changes to the submit/signIn payload construction or to the zod schema/resolver wiring that typically determines which fields are passed through. If the existing submit path only sends the previously validated fields (common with `zodResolver`), `credentials.backupCode` will never be provided, so the provider will always take the TOTP path (`else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)`) and the new IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes branches in `login.tsx` would be unreachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single-use backup-code enforcement is a check-then-act race with no transaction, row lock, or atomic compare-and-update: two concurrent sign-ins with the same code can both pass `indexOf` before either write lands (one single-use code grants two logins), and two different codes used in parallel mean last-write-wins resurrects an already-consumed code

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login does `indexOf(credentials.backupCode...)` on a decrypted array and then performs a separate `prisma.user.update` that rewrites the whole `backupCodes` blob (`backupCodes[index] = null` then re-encrypt). There’s no transaction, row lock, or atomic conditional update tying the read to the write, so two concurrent sign-ins can both pass the `indexOf` check before either update commits, allowing reuse of a “single-use” code. Likewise, two different codes used concurrently can cause last-write-wins on the full-array rewrite, potentially reintroducing a code that the other request nulled out.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Clipboard copy in `EnableTwoFactorModal` (`backup-codes-copy` onClick) has no error handling: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is neither awaited nor caught and the success toast fires unconditionally — on permission denial the promise rejects unhandled while the toast falsely claims success, and on insecure (plain-HTTP) contexts `navigator.clipboard` is undefined causing a synchronous throw with no toast at all

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal` under `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, the `backup-codes-copy` button’s `onClick` calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without `await`/`.then` and without `try/catch`, and immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` unconditionally. From the diff this can (a) show a success toast even if the clipboard write is denied/rejected, and (b) throw synchronously if `navigator.clipboard` is undefined (e.g., non-secure context), with no user feedback and a potential unhandled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No re-display or regeneration path for backup codes: codes are minted only in `setup.ts` and displayed exactly once in client state, so closing the dialog via X/Esc/backdrop or refreshing after `handleEnable` permanently loses unsaved codes; the `MissingBackupCodes` message tells users to generate codes in settings but no code implements this, creating an unrecoverable lockout for accounts with `backupCodes = null` (and pre-deploy 2FA users)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup codes are generated only in `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` and sent to the client once (`return res.json({ ..., backupCodes })`), then only kept in `EnableTwoFactorModal` component state (`setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)`) and displayed in the `DisplayBackupCodes` step. There is no endpoint/UI in this diff to re-fetch or regenerate existing backup codes later, yet user-facing strings include `missing_backup_codes`: "Please generate them in your settings." The diff does not implement any “generate backup codes” action in settings beyond the initial setup flow. This is a real product/edge-case gap (especially for users with `twoFactorEnabled` but `backupCodes` null) but not a strictly verifiable broken behavior, since users can still use TOTP when backup codes are missing; the lockout scenario depends on user circumstances (lost authenticator) and unshown UX flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dialog-dismissal paths never reset modal state: `resetForm`/`resetState` are only wired to explicit toggle and Close/Cancel buttons, so Esc, backdrop, X, or the Disable modal's Cancel leave `twoFactorLostAccess`, `errorMessage`, form values, and `step` stale, making reopening show the wrong mode or stale errors; at `DisplayBackupCodes`, X/Esc skip `onEnable()`, leaving the parent switch rendering "off" while 2FA is actually enabled until a refresh

adjudication.rationale: In both modals, state reset is only wired to specific button handlers, not to dialog dismissal. `EnableTwoFactorModal` defines `resetState()` but only calls it on the Cancel button (not shown during `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`) and the explicit `backup-codes-close` button; it does not reset on `onOpenChange` when the dialog closes via Esc/backdrop/X. Also, after successful enable, it sets `step` to `DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()` (`handleEnable` success path), so if the user closes the dialog via Esc/backdrop/X during the backup-codes step, `onEnable()` won’t run, leaving the parent potentially stale even though 2FA is enabled server-side. `DisableTwoFactorModal` similarly has `resetForm`/`setTwoFactorLostAccess(false)` only on success or the lost-access toggle; the Cancel button just calls `onCancel` without clearing `twoFactorLostAccess`, `errorMessage`, or form values, so reopening can show stale mode/errors/inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing-encryption-key path in `disable.ts` throws `new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` instead of returning a JSON error, producing a Next.js 500 with a non-JSON body so the client's `await response.json()` throws and the user gets the generic catch-all instead of a mapped error

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch checks `if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` and then `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);` instead of returning `res.status(...).json(...)`. A thrown error in a Next.js API route typically results in a 500 response that may not have a JSON body. On the client, `DisableTwoFactorModal.handleDisable` unconditionally does `const body = await response.json();` for non-200 responses inside a try block; if the response isn't valid JSON, `response.json()` will throw and the code will fall into the catch-all error handling rather than mapping `InternalServerError` (or any specific error) to a user-facing message. This problematic path is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.replaceAll()` on unvalidated user input in `disable.ts` (and the same pattern in `next-auth-options.ts`) can crash the endpoint with a 500: `req.body.backupCode` is used directly as a string with no type check or schema validation, so a body like `{"backupCode": 123}` throws a TypeError instead of returning a 400

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path checks only truthiness (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`) and then calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If a client sends a non-string truthy value like `{ "backupCode": 123 }`, `replaceAll` will throw a `TypeError` and the endpoint will 500 instead of returning a 400. This is a real, diff-grounded crash bug on malformed input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive backup-code comparison with no input normalization: codes are lowercase hex but the input lacks `autoCapitalize="none"`/normalization and the placeholder is uppercase, so iOS Safari's default sentence autocapitalization causes a hand-typed valid code to fail with "Backup code is incorrect" in the one-shot recovery flow

adjudication_records.issue_text: Null-hole consumption representation conflates 'missing' with 'exhausted': consumed codes become null placeholders in a JSON blob, so once all 10 are used the column is a truthy string, MissingBackupCodes can never fire again, and exhausted users get 'Backup code is incorrect.'

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, verified backup codes are “consumed” by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting the JSON array back into `user.backupCodes`. Because `MissingBackupCodes` is only thrown when `!user.backupCodes` (i.e., DB column is null/empty), an exhausted set (all entries `null`) still leaves a truthy encrypted string in the column, so `MissingBackupCodes` will never trigger for exhaustion. Subsequent attempts will hit `indexOf(...) === -1` and throw/return `IncorrectBackupCode`, conflating exhausted vs missing as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: One-time-use guarantee is not atomic (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:143-158): the consume step is decrypt → indexOf → set the entry to null → re-encrypt the whole array → user.update, with no transaction or conditional write. Concurrent sign-ins with the same code can both pass indexOf before either writes (classic TOCTOU, code used twice), and concurrent sign-ins with different codes each serialize a full stale array so the second write resurrects the code the first just consumed, violating the locale string's 'Each backup code can be used exactly once' promise. Fix with a transaction plus conditional update, or store one row per code with an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE code = x AND used = false.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts, the backup-code consume flow is: decrypt stored array → indexOf(user input) → set backupCodes[index] = null → prisma.user.update({ backupCodes: encrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes)) }). This is a read-modify-write with no transaction/locking or conditional update, so concurrent sign-ins can both pass the indexOf check before either update (same code used twice), and concurrent updates for different codes can overwrite each other with stale arrays (lost update), potentially “resurrecting” a code that another request just nulled. That violates the stated one-time-use guarantee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is burned before authentication completes (next-auth-options.ts:149-158): the destructive user.update runs immediately after the code matches, but authorize must still return and next-auth must complete session/JWT creation (plus any later checks such as rate limiting or org/email-verification) — any failure after the burn consumes one of the 10 limited codes without granting access. Consume the code only after the full sign-in succeeds, or accept and document the lossy semantics.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup-code path mutates persistent state immediately upon a match: it sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and runs `await prisma.user.update(...)` inside `authorize` before `authorize` has successfully completed and returned the user. Since execution continues after this block (no early return shown), any later failure/throw within `authorize` (or any sign-in failure before NextAuth completes the flow) would consume a one-time backup code without granting access. That is lossy behavior and can lead to user-facing data loss of backup codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race in backup code burn: non-atomic read-modify-write (indexOf → set to null → re-encrypt → prisma.user.update) allows two concurrent sign-ins with the same code to both succeed, violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee — needs a conditional/atomic update so only one request wins

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code consumption is implemented as: decrypt `user.backupCodes` → `indexOf(credentials.backupCode...)` → set `backupCodes[index] = null` → `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) }})`. This is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no conditional/transactional guard tying the update to the previously-read value, so two concurrent authorize calls using the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either update commits, allowing the same code to be accepted twice and violating the “used exactly once” guarantee added by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is consumed inside authorize() before the session/JWT/cookie is actually created — if anything fails after the burn (JWT/session callbacks, dropped response, cookie not persisted), the user is not logged in but the code is destroyed, and retrying yields IncorrectBackupCode for a valid code; consumption should be tied to actual sign-in completion or be retriable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup code is invalidated inside the CredentialsProvider `authorize()` flow: after matching, it does `backupCodes[index] = null` and immediately persists the updated encrypted list via `prisma.user.update(...)`. This happens before NextAuth finishes the sign-in lifecycle (JWT/session callbacks and response/cookie persistence occur after `authorize()` returns). If sign-in fails or the response/cookie isn’t persisted after this DB write, the user won’t be logged in but the backup code has already been consumed, making a retry return `IncorrectBackupCode` for what was valid at the time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message tells users to 'generate them in your settings' but no backup code regeneration endpoint/UI exists in the PR — users who enabled 2FA before the migration have backupCodes = NULL (nullable column, no backfill) and can never obtain codes, and codes are shown only once in EnableTwoFactorModal with no way to re-view them

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nullable `users.backupCodes` column with no backfill (migration only `ADD COLUMN ... TEXT;`). Backup codes are only generated in `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` during the enable flow and are only displayed once in `EnableTwoFactorModal` (step `DisplayBackupCodes`), with no UI/endpoint in this diff to regenerate or re-view them later. Meanwhile, both login (`next-auth-options.ts`) and disable (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`) implement backup-code paths that return/throw `MissingBackupCodes` when `user.backupCodes` is null, and the UI shows the message “Please generate them in your settings.” Since this PR also adds “Lost access” toggles that route users to the backup code input (`Login` and `DisableTwoFactorModal`), existing 2FA users who predate the migration (backupCodes = NULL) can hit a dead-end with no way provided by this diff to obtain codes, potentially preventing account access if they’ve lost their authenticator.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EnableTwoFactorModal state is only reset via Cancel/Close footer buttons — dismissal via X button, Escape, or overlay click passes through onOpenChange leaving stale step/password/backupCodes/secret state, and X-dismissal after successful enable skips onEnable() so the parent thinks 2FA is disabled and re-running setup silently rotates the already-saved codes

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, internal state (step/password/errorMessage and also backupCodes/dataUri/secret/backupCodesUrl) is only reset in footer button handlers: Cancel calls onCancel()+resetState(), and the DisplayBackupCodes “close” calls resetState()+onEnable(). But the Dialog is controlled via <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}> and there is no wrapper onOpenChange handler or effect to reset state when the user dismisses via the dialog’s X/Escape/overlay. That can leave the modal reopening on a stale step with stale sensitive values. Additionally, after a successful enable (handleEnable sets step=DisplayBackupCodes and does not call onEnable), dismissing the dialog via X/Escape/overlay would skip onEnable(), so the parent won’t be notified even though 2FA was enabled; rerunning setup would hit /totp/setup again which (per diff) generates and persists new backupCodes, silently rotating them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: E2e assertion always passes: `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise object which is always truthy, so the '2FA is enabled' check passes instantly whether or not the switch is checked — should use toBeChecked() instead

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the assertion `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` is asserting on the Promise returned by `isChecked()`, which is always truthy as an object, so it can pass even when the switch is not checked. adjudication_records.issue_text: Unvalidated req.body.backupCode crashes the disable endpoint: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes a string, so a JSON body like {"backupCode": 5} throws a TypeError and returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 validation error

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path does `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode` is truthy. There is no type check that `req.body.backupCode` is a string, so a request body like `{ "backupCode": 5 }` would enter this branch and `replaceAll` would throw a `TypeError` (since numbers don’t have `replaceAll`), resulting in an unhandled 500 rather than a controlled 400 error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code input is not normalized for case and whitespace — server only strips dashes with no .toLowerCase() or .trim(), so uppercase entry (invited by the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder) or paper-transcribed/pasted codes with stray whitespace are falsely rejected as 'Backup code is incorrect'

adjudication.rationale: In both the disable API (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`) and NextAuth authorize (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`), backup code verification uses `indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` / `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` with no `.trim()` or case normalization. Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`), while the UI placeholder is `"XXXXX-XXXXX"` (suggesting uppercase) and users may paste with whitespace. Uppercased A-F or stray spaces would be falsely rejected as `IncorrectBackupCode`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy button shows the 'Copied!' success toast unconditionally — navigator.clipboard.writeText is fire-and-forget and showToast runs immediately regardless of rejection (insecure context, missing permissions, unavailable clipboard API), falsely telling the user codes are saved with no way to view them again

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, the copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` and immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` without `await`/`.then`/`.catch` or checking `navigator.clipboard` availability. If the clipboard API is unavailable or the promise rejects (permissions/insecure context), the UI will still show a success toast, which is incorrect behavior.
